targets.from: pipeline/tree_cards.py from the research record (crown: About 7 spreading leaves (Henderson); 5-8 arching leaves forming a plumose crown (Mori et al. 1997). Mori calls it a canopy palm. 'open' density follows from the leaf count, not a stated value.), no photographs measured

description: A palm of lowland rain forest, secondary/gaps, 15-20 m tall (to 25 m). Stilt roots up to 25, widely spaced in a loose open cone, diagonal, branched near or below ground, terete, 1-2(-4) m long and to 9 cm thick, brown turning black, with spines to 2 cm (stem itself smooth). About 7 spreading leaves (Henderson); 5-8 arching leaves forming a plumose crown (Mori et al. Fruit: ovoid-cylindric, 2.5-3.5 x 1.5-2 cm, epicarp yellowish at maturity, splitting from the apex; seed 1.5-2.5 x 1-1.5 cm.

range.where: Nicaragua south to Bolivia and east through Venezuela, the Guianas and Brazil

notes: Template palm: a palm: Corner's model (one unbranched stem, a crown of large leaves at its top), the palm block from the research's. Crown width: twice the frond length, the fronds arching (no source gives the crown's width). Leaf size clamped to 0.6 m (the source's 65 cm is past what a leaf card carries). NOT SOURCED (the template's or a default value): leaf colour (a tropical evergreen's mid green); the pinnae's hang (a little: droop 0.15); leaf-scar ring spacing (15 cm). Research notes: Height: Wikipedia typically 15-20, to 25 m; Henderson to 20 m, usually less; UTP 8-25 m. Stem diameter: Wikipedia typically about 12, to 16 cm. Leaves: UTP about 7, 1.5-2 m long; leaf.length_cm is the rachis (Henderson 1.4-2.8 m), and the petiole adds 15-40 cm. Pinnae: Henderson to 90 x 20 cm, Mori to 100 x 30 cm; 40 cm is the proximal pinna. 'secondary/gaps' comes from UTP ('common in non-flooded fields and fallows'), and evergreen is assumed for a palm, not stated. Mori: on all soil and drainage types in French Guiana, never dense. Phenology: Wikipedia says flowering is mostly in the dry season (no region given); Mori: flowers and fruits year-round (French Guiana). No Madre de Dios or Osa months found. Fruit is yellow and edible (Wikipedia). White-lipped peccaries eat many seeds (Wikipedia); collared peccaries damage stilt-root tips (Spanish Wikipedia). The Napo camera-trap study covered Socratea spp. only. Palmweb blocked automated fetches.
